title.narrative: Strengthened capacity of member States to ratify and apply international labour standards and to fulfil their reporting obligations

description.narrative: The Indonesian Government’s efforts to foster a conducive environment for investment culminated in the enactment of the Omnibus Law on Job Creation in 2020 and its amendment in 2023. This legislation introduced a broad array of reforms across various domains, including labour regulation. However, the primary challenge remains the effective implementation of both international labour standards (ILS) and national labour laws. Full compliance with ratified International Labour Organization (ILO) Conventions is essential to achieving decent work. In this regard, Indonesia’s labour market and industrial relations would greatly benefit from improved enforcement and adherence to these standards. Supporting tripartite consultations, as mandated by ILO Convention No. 144 on tripartite consultation, is critical. These consultations can enhance the quality and timeliness of national reports submitted on ratified conventions and help address comments from ILO supervisory bodies. Furthermore, such support could pave the way for tripartite consensus on the ratification of additional Conventions recommended under the ILO Special Review Mechanism. The ILO will continue to advocate for the ratification and implementation of key conventions, particularly: • Convention No. 155 (Occupational Safety and Health), as it is part of the Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work. • Convention No. 122 (Employment Policy) and Convention No. 129 (Labour Inspection in Agriculture), both of which are recognized as governance conventions. Additionally, the ILO will promote several technical conventions, including: • Convention No. 176 (Occupational Safety and Health in Mining), • Convention No. 188 (Work in Fishing), • Convention No. 189 (Decent Work for Domestic Workers), and • Convention No. 190 (Violence and Harassment at Work). Ratifying and implementing these conventions would further strengthen Indonesia’s commitment to decent work and align the country with global labour standards.
